items.followUp: Write the HTML code to add a horizontal line below the word “Welcome”.

rubric.why: The horizontal-rule tag is the HTML element used to add a horizontal line.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for <hr> or the self-closing form <hr />.

items.followUp: Write HTML code to make the word “computer” bold.

rubric.why: The word must be enclosed in an HTML tag that displays it in italics.
rubric.description: Uses an italic or emphasis tag around “student”.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a correctly formed <i> or <em> element containing student.

items.followUp: Write the steps for creating and viewing a simple webpage.

rubric.why: A webpage is created by entering HTML code in a text or HTML editor.
rubric.description: Identifies using an editor to write the webpage code.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming an editor such as Notepad or an HTML editor.

rubric.why: Saving the file with an HTML extension allows it to be opened and viewed in a web browser.
rubric.description: Saves the webpage as an HTML file and views it in a browser.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the file is saved with an .html extension and opened in a browser.

modelAnswer: Open a text editor, such as Notepad, and type the HTML code.
Save the file with an .html extension, then open it in a web browser.

rubric.why: Web surfing means browsing or navigating websites on the internet.
rubric.description: Defines web surfing as browsing or navigating websites on the internet.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for identifying the activity as browsing or navigating websites on the internet.

modelAnswer: Web surfing is the activity of browsing or navigating different websites on the internet.

items.followUp: What is test data? Name and briefly describe three types of test data.

rubric.why: Test data is entered to check whether a program or system works correctly.
rubric.description: Defines test data as data used to test a program or system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that data is used to test a program or system.

rubric.why: Normal data is valid data within the expected range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming normal data.

rubric.why: Extreme data is at the limit of the acceptable range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming extreme data.

rubric.why: Abnormal data is invalid or outside the acceptable range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming abnormal or invalid data.

modelAnswer: Test data is data entered into a program to check whether it works correctly.
Normal data is valid data within the expected range.
Extreme data is valid data at the limit of the acceptable range.
Abnormal data is invalid data outside the acceptable range.

items.followUp: Define TCP/IP and describe the Internet and Network Access layers.

rubric.why: TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol and is the suite of rules used for communication over networks, including the internet.
rubric.description: Gives the full form of TCP/IP and its role in network communication.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct full form and explaining that it provides rules for communication or data transfer over networks.

rubric.why: The Application layer provides network services to user applications.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it provides network services to applications or users.

rubric.why: The Transport layer supports end-to-end delivery of data between devices or applications.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its role in end-to-end data delivery.

modelAnswer: TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol; it is a suite of rules that enables communication and data transfer over networks.
The Application layer provides network services to user applications.
The Transport layer is responsible for end-to-end delivery of data.

items.followUp: What is encryption, and how does it help protect online information?

rubric.why: Encryption converts readable information into coded or unreadable form so that unauthorised people cannot easily understand it.
rubric.description: Explains encryption as converting readable data into coded or unreadable data.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for describing the conversion of readable information into coded or unreadable form.

rubric.why: Encryption protects sensitive information from unauthorised access and helps keep online communications or transactions secure.
rubric.description: Explains the importance of encryption for protecting online information.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for explaining that encryption prevents unauthorised access or protects sensitive online data or transactions.

modelAnswer: Encryption is the process of converting readable data into coded, unreadable form.
It helps prevent unauthorised people from reading sensitive information and keeps online communication and transactions secure.

items.followUp: What does the decision symbol show in a flowchart, and what paths can follow it?

rubric.why: A decision symbol represents a condition or question that must be evaluated.
rubric.description: States that the symbol represents a condition or decision.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a condition, decision, or question.

rubric.why: The result of the decision determines which branch is followed, commonly labelled Yes/No or True/False.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving Yes/No or True/False as the branches.

modelAnswer: The decision symbol represents a condition or question in a flowchart.
It divides the flow into branches, usually labelled Yes/No or True/False.
